name: Major cyber incidents
summary: Second wave of refrigeration-control attacks hit EU supermarkets; Binance theft largest on record
state: Attackers reset internet-exposed refrigeration controllers at supermarkets in several European countries around 2 Nov, a second wave after attacks on about 700 French stores in mid-October, forcing stores to discard food (The Hacker News; ITV). The FBI attributes the roughly $6.3bn Binance theft to North Korea. No national-scale outage of power, health or finance systems was reported as of 6 Nov.
for_you: Follow NCSC guidance on securing internet-connected devices and accounts.
rubric_hit: Attack disrupting large companies across several countries = Watch

sources.title: The Hacker News — Second wave of cyberattacks hits supermarkets
ITV News — Cyberattack hits 700 supermarkets in France

why: Ransomware and state hacking now shut down hospitals, retailers, carmakers and airports for weeks.
drivers: Ransomware gangs, state actors, zero-days, supply-chain compromises.

rubric.alert: National-scale attack on critical infrastructure (power, health, finance), or a destructive state-attributed attack.
rubric.watch: Ransomware or attack disrupting a large company or critical service, or a mass-exploited zero-day.
rubric.normal: No major incidents disrupting critical services this week.
